bullets.title: NVDA Feynman GPU Ahead of Schedule on TSMC A16; Supply Chain Mobilizing for 2028
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm NVIDIA's next-next-gen 'Feynman' platform is ahead of schedule, targeting H2 2028 mass production using TSMC's A16 (upgraded 2nm) process with co-packaged optics (CPO) and higher SoIC 3D stacking. DigiTimes and fintwit analysts flag this as a supply-chain alignment event: TSM on SiPh fab, LITE on ELS/high-power lasers, FN on CPO assembly, COHR on optical components, and GLW on materials. Samsung's Giheung R&D fab is also being utilized by NVDA to meet near-term demand.

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics Now in Full Production; LITE, COHR, TSM, FN Key Suppliers
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics scale-out networking infrastructure has entered full production, with a well-mapped supply chain: TSM (silicon photonics fab/COUPE), LITE (ELS, high-power lasers, optical alignment & test), COHR (ELS + optical components), GLW (fiber/connectors), FN (switch CPO assembly & test). A 19-company coalition led by Lightmatter has also launched an Open Silicon Photonics initiative within OCP, publishing a ~300-page architecture paper for interoperable CPO-based AI infrastructure, involving CLS, DELL, and QBTS.

bullets.title: LITE Post-Earnings: Beat Guidance, EPS Above, But Stock Sold Off 8%
bullets.body: COHR beat Q4 FY26 with $2.05B revenue (+34% YoY, +13.3% QoQ), while LITE's earnings call was called 'one of the most interesting' by multiple analysts, with the stock seen as 'one of the defining stocks of this cycle.' Fintwit noted COHR generates 2x LITE revenue but trades at $10B lower valuation due to different product mix/margins. Multiple accounts flagged COHR's 8% post-earnings selloff as a disconnect vs. strong results, while enthusiasm for LITE's scale-out demand trajectory remains high.

bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day: HBF Architecture Delivers 8-16x Capacity; Flash Market to 1.2ZB in 2026
bullets.body: SanDisk's 2026 Investor Day highlighted the HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) architecture delivering 8-16x capacity at comparable cost, with flash market estimated to reach ~1.2 zettabytes of shipments in 2026. Datacenter expected to reach ~50% of industry bits and overtake edge as largest end market. Multiple fintwit accounts remain long SNDK, citing HBF/HBM context and SK Hynix/Google customer pursuit. One account noted SNDK has low SBC-to-FCF ratio relative to peers.

bullets.title: INTC: $20B Offering Upsizes on $100B+ Institutional Demand; GF Securities Buy at $136 PT
bullets.body: Intel's $20B share offering was upsized from $15B at $95/share (~2.6% discount), with institutional demand exceeding $100B. CEO subscribed ~$12M personally. GF Securities reiterates Buy with $136 price target, viewing the offering as positive for management confidence in 18A foundry and EMIB strategy. $2.2M above-ask call sweep targeted the $135 strike. Hedgeye also flagged INTC back to bullish TREND.

bullets.title: RDDT Confirmed for S&P 500 Inclusion Aug. 18; Replaces AvalonBay
bullets.body: S&P Dow Jones Indices confirmed Reddit (RDDT) will replace AvalonBay Communities in the S&P 500, effective prior to open on August 18. AvalonBay is being acquired by Equity Residential. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged the catalyst as meaningful for forced passive buying.

bullets.title: PLTR: Unusual OTM Call Sweep Ahead of Close; AI Control-Plane Thesis Strengthens
bullets.body: Millions in OTM PLTR calls were accumulating ahead of the close per options flow trackers. Separately, one analyst argued that as AI model costs converge and commoditize, third-party control planes like Palantir are positioned as the next competitive battleground—enabling quasi-interchangeable model deployment across vendors.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Hits Record 7,800 for First Time; QQQ on Track for 2nd-Best August This Century
bullets.body: The S&P 500 crossed 7,800 for the first time—its 27th all-time high of the year and 470th since 2013—driven by back-to-back soft inflation prints (CPI/PPI). Nasdaq 100 gained 1.1% and is tracking for its 2nd-best August this century. Market breadth improved: 73% of Nasdaq 100 constituents trade above their 200-day MA, the best reading in 13 months. Rate hike odds fell to 31%.

bullets.title: SPY Gamma Dynamics: $8.6B Positive Gamma at 780; Vol Crushed to 7% IV
bullets.body: SPY has $8.6 billion in positive gamma exposure at the 780 strike—described as 'unprecedented' and acting as a price magnet. Volatility has been crushed with Monday IV at 7% (rank 7/100) and call skew at 99/100, creating vanna support. Analyst expects vol subdued 4-5 sessions, with OPEX next week the first opportunity to re-bid volatility.

bullets.title: AAPL Opens Houston Advanced Manufacturing Center; Mac Mini and AI Servers Go Domestic
bullets.body: Apple opened an Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, investing hundreds of millions. The facility will begin Mac mini production this year and has already shipped first advanced AI servers domestically. Apple is also seeking regulatory compensation for platform services in an ongoing dispute. Apple and Alibaba reportedly co-developed a China-specific LLM rather than licensing Alibaba's model as-is.

bullets.title: GOOGL Capital Allocation: TPU/AI Datacenter ROIC Seen Beating Gemini Model Investment
bullets.body: One analyst argued Google should prioritize TPU/AI datacenter capex over continued Gemini model development, citing superior ROIC and accelerated first-year bonus depreciation benefits. Baupost's Q2 13F shows GOOGL as a top-5 position at $484.7M.

bullets.title: NVDA Burry Short Doubles Down; $500B AI Deal Compared to Enron
bullets.body: Michael Burry has doubled his NVDA short position, warning that the $500B AI financing initiative has 'shades of Enron.' Goldman Sachs is separately reported to be in talks to join NVDA's $500B AI financing program, suggesting institutional backing. LG is adopting NVIDIA Isaac Groot for next-gen humanoid robots, and NVDA showed the most bullish options flow on the day.

bullets.title: AMD Raises $4.75B in Largest-Ever Bond Offering; ASIC Startups Locked Out of HBM/CoWoS
bullets.body: AMD completed its largest-ever U.S. dollar bond offering at $4.75B. Separately, analysts note ASIC startups cannot secure sufficient HBM and CoWoS capacity as hyperscalers and GPU designers (AMD, NVIDIA) have monopolized available supply. AMD also released a video highlighting partnership with Cerebras.

bullets.title: PI (Impinj) Gets Double Upgrade on QLC SSD Demand Finally Materializing
bullets.body: Susquehanna upgraded PI from Neutral to Positive with PT raised from $85 to $120; Morgan Stanley upgraded from Equal Weight to Overweight with PT raised from $87 to $108. Both cite QLC mass-capacity SSD demand 'finally beginning to materialize following nearly a year of delays.'

bullets.title: Tesla FSD Praised; Robotaxi Wait Times Improve in Austin
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts retweeted enthusiastic Tesla FSD endorsements: FSD 14.3.7 described as 'quite a beautiful build,' HW4 praised as 'mind-blowing.' Austin Robotaxi wait times reportedly improved significantly from prior 20-minute waits. One user claims Tesla saved their life. Elon Musk retweeted praise for Tesla multimodal AI capabilities.

bullets.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.22%, Highest Since 2001; US National Debt Up $3.7T in 13 Months
bullets.body: The $25B 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.216-5.22%, the highest yield since auctions resumed after a near-five-year suspension and the highest since August 2001. US national debt increased $3.7T over 13 months. Fitch affirmed US at AA+ with stable outlook but warned fiscal pressures will increase as Medicare/Social Security spending expands ~1ppt of GDP by 2032.

bullets.title: TSMC A16 Process: Skip 2nm, Direct to 1.6nm; SoIC 3D Stacking and Custom HBM/CPO Integration
bullets.body: Reports from DigiTimes and fintwit analysts indicate TSMC is advancing directly to A16 (upgraded 2nm process), skipping standard 2nm. A16 will feature increased SoIC 3D stacking and integration of custom HBM and CPO on top. TSMC is ramping full speed to meet Nvidia Feynman's 2028 target.

bullets.title: NFLX at Largest Premium to 50-Day MA Since April; DIS, ORCL, INTU at 200-Week MA
bullets.body: Netflix is on track to close at its largest premium to the 50-day moving average since April, per technical analysts. Separately, ORCL, NFLX, DIS, and INTU were flagged as trading at or near their 200-week moving averages—a historically significant technical support zone.

bullets.title: CSCO Disappoints on AI Data-Center Outlook; NOW Up 47%
bullets.body: Cisco disappointed with its AI data-center sales projection per corporate news flow, with the stock declining. ServiceNow (NOW) was up 47% over a recent period according to multiple fintwit posts. Workday (WDAY) surged on reports Silver Lake is evaluating a ~$43B acquisition.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI Capex Borrowing Reshapes Foreign Credit Markets; Amazon Builds 400-450MW Datacenter Campus Near Gilroy
bullets.body: FT reports hyperscalers' AI infrastructure spending is driving a global debt issuance boom, reshaping foreign credit markets. On the ground, Amazon is building three data centers totaling ~400-450MW near Gilroy, California. AI infrastructure positions bought at late-July lows have averaged +28.7% in roughly two weeks per one analyst.
